issue.title: sase-telegram test_telegram_submits_a_shell_backed_gate calls create_gate with a rowless shell block, refused since c6807d24c
issue.description: Proposed by phase bead sase-16n.9 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1) and triaged by the sase-16n land agent. In the linked sase-telegram repo, tests/test_gate_shell_settlement.py::test_telegram_submits_a_shell_backed_gate fails on a clean tree (sase-16n.9 reproduced with its changes stashed). Root cause: the test builds a custom-kind spec with a shell block (_spec(..., shell=True)) and passes it straight to sase.notification_gates.service.create_gate. Host commit c6807d24c (fix(gate): refuse rowless shell-block custom gates) made validate_gate_spec (src/sase/notification_gates/validation.py:67-70) raise missing_gate_shell_row for any custom spec with a shell block that lacks shell_row_managed=True, which only the gate-shell transaction sets. Fix the test to create the gate through the supported gate-shell path (sase.gate_shell create_gate_shell / transaction) or set shell_row_managed explicitly when it builds its own member row with _make_gate_shell_member; do not weaken the host guard. Then run the sase-telegram check recipe via sase tool run check.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic host validation refusal: every run of create_gate with a rowless custom shell spec raises missing_gate_shell_row; sase-16n.9 saw it fail identically on a clean sase-telegram tree.
